paper_metadata.title: Quantum speedup for combinatorial optimization with flat energy landscapes

experiments.description: Optimized quantum adiabatic algorithm (QAA) on hard Maximum Independent Set unit-disk graph instances, analyzed theoretically via perturbation theory and exact/DMRG gap calculations.

algorithm.variant: optimized QAA for Maximum Independent Set
algorithm.convergence_criteria: adiabatic evolution optimized to minimize runtime while maintaining adiabaticity near the minimum gap

hyperparameters.U: U >> |delta| (independent-set violation penalty; often taken to infinity in analysis)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per graph vertex; computational basis states encode independent sets
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize independent set size, equivalently minimize H_cost = -delta sum_u n_u + U sum_(u,v in E) n_u n_v
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: penalty term U >> |delta| enforces independent-set constraint
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_QAA = H_cost - H_q, with H_q = Omega sum_u (|1_u><0_u| + h.c.)

problem_instance.description: Hard unit-disk graph instances with flat low-energy landscapes; includes a family of star graphs with nb branches of even length ell and random 80% filled unit-disk graphs up to 460 vertices for runtime studies, and up to 80 vertices for DMRG gap studies.

dataset_specification.description: Randomly generated unit-disk graphs embedded on a 2D square lattice with 80% filling; 1000 instances per system size up to 720 vertices in Appendix B; top 5% hardest instances used in several plots; star-graph family analyzed separately.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: enumeration of independent sets and perturbative construction of effective Hamiltonians
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: gap extraction and runtime scaling analysis

results.unit: runtime lower bound, scales as max_b D_{b-1}/D_b up to polynomial factors
runtime to find an optimal solution with probability 3/4
optimized adiabatic runtime proportional to Delta_QAA^-1

classical_baselines.unit: runtime lower bound, scales as max_b D_{b-1}/D_b up to polynomial factors
runtime to find an optimal solution with probability 3/4

speedup_claims.conditions: when low-energy eigenstates are delocalized on flat energy landscapes; optimized adiabatic evolution near the minimum gap
speedup_claims.caveats: instance-dependent; can become a slowdown if eigenstates are unfavorably localized

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(Delta_QAA^-1) under optimized adiabatic evolution; for delocalized instances Delta_QAA ~ Omega_alpha sqrt(D_alpha/D_{alpha-1})
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: SA lower bound scales as Omega(max_b D_{b-1}/D_b) up to polynomial factors; for studied unit-disk graphs exponential in sqrt(n)

experiments.description: Modified QAA with an added local delocalizing Hamiltonian H_ell, evaluated on hard Maximum Independent Set unit-disk graph instances to obtain a quadratic speedup over classical Markov-chain methods.

algorithm.variant: modified QAA with delocalizing Hamiltonian H_ell
algorithm.convergence_criteria: adiabatic evolution with lambda chosen large enough to enforce delocalization in the relevant manifolds

hyperparameters.lambda: time-independent energy scale multiplying H_ell; examples include lambda/Omega = 5 and lambda/Omega = 1 in numerics

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per vertex; H_ell acts within independent-set manifolds defined by spin exchanges
problem_formulation.objective_function: same MIS objective as exp_1, with added delocalizing term to favor uniform superpositions within each independent-set size
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: penalty U for constraint violations; H_ell constructed from local graph information
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = H_QAA + lambda H_ell, where H_ell = -H_se + diagonal degree term

problem_instance.description: Hard unit-disk graph instances from the same family as exp_1; numerical study on top 1% hardest instances up to n = 80 and broader scaling up to n = 460; also star graphs with branch lengths ell = 4, 6, 8.

dataset_specification.description: Top 1% hardest unit-disk graph instances for DMRG studies; top 5% hardest for gap-gap scaling; star-graph family used as a structured test case.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: construct H_ell from local graph structure; compute restricted-manifold gaps Delta_{ell,b}
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: compare Delta_QAA^{-1} against SA lower bounds and extract scaling

results.unit: 1/n (typical lower bound stated as > 1/n for most instances)

classical_baselines.unit: max_b D_{b-1}/D_b up to polynomial factors
max_b D_{b-1}/D_b up to polynomial factors
max_b D_{b-1}/(e_max D_b) up to polynomial factors

speedup_claims.baseline_method: simulated annealing, parallel tempering, and path-integral quantum Monte Carlo
speedup_claims.conditions: when the added delocalizing Hamiltonian H_ell enforces delocalization in the relevant manifolds; lambda sufficiently large (e.g. lambda/Omega = 5 in numerics)
speedup_claims.caveats: QMC can match only if the restricted Gibbs distribution is exponentially favorably localized, which would also favor QAA; speedup is proven for a wide class of QMC algorithms, not all possible variants

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: quadratic speedup over SA/QMC in favorable delocalization regime; Delta_QAA ~ Omega_alpha sqrt(D_alpha/D_{alpha-1}) in the lambda -> infinity limit
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: SA and QMC lower bounds scale like max_b D_{b-1}/D_b up to polynomial factors

experiments.description: Star-graph benchmark showing how QAA runtime changes from quadratic speedup to slowdown as the suboptimal eigenstate localizes with increasing branch length.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: adiabatic evolution near the avoided crossing

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per vertex on a star graph with nb branches of even length ell
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximum Independent Set on star graphs
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: penalty U for violating independent-set constraints

problem_instance.description: Family of star graphs with nb branches of even length ell; unique optimal independent set and many suboptimal size alpha-1 configurations with domain walls.

dataset_specification.description: Structured graph family used to illustrate delocalized vs localized low-energy eigenstates; no external dataset.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: symmetrization over branches; perturbative construction of |G> and |E>
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: compare predicted and exact gaps and scaling with nb

results.unit: power-law exponent relative to SA lower bound in delocalized case
power-law exponent relative to SA lower bound in localized case
Delta_QAA decreases exponentially in nb for fixed ell

speedup_claims.conditions: for ell = 2, where the first excited state delocalizes evenly among domain-wall configurations
speedup_claims.caveats: as ell increases, the first excited state localizes and QAA can become slower than SA
runtime can scale as tau_SA^{3/2} in the localized regime

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: For ell = 2, Delta_QAA^{-1} ~ sqrt(tau_SA); for larger ell, Delta_QAA^{-1} can become worse than SA and scale as tau_SA^{3/2} in the localized regime
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: SA lower bound scales as (ell/2 + 1)^{nb} up to polynomial factors

experiments.description: Numerical study of the modified QAA at finite lambda on hard unit-disk graph instances, showing that modest lambda values preserve the quadratic speedup.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: ground and first excited states converged in DMRG; truncation error below 1e-8

hyperparameters.V: 10 energy penalty used to compute first excited state via H' = H + V|psi0><psi0|

problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximum Independent Set on unit-disk graphs with added delocalizing Hamiltonian
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: large penalty U on independent-set violations

problem_instance.description: Top 1% hardest unit-disk graph instances up to n = 80 vertices; compared against SA lower bounds.

dataset_specification.description: Hardest instances selected by SA lower bound; DMRG used to compute Delta_QAA for each instance and lambda setting.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: construct Hamiltonian; compute ground state and first excited state with penalty method

classical_baselines.unit: max_b D_{b-1}/D_b up to polynomial factors

speedup_claims.conditions: for the studied top 1% hardest unit-disk graph instances up to n = 80, with lambda = 1 or 5
speedup_claims.caveats: speedup is shown numerically via DMRG; modest lambda values suffice on the studied instances

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: quadratic speedup over SA for lambda = 1 or 5 on the studied instances
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: SA lower bound from max_b D_{b-1}/D_b

experiments.description: Perturbative analysis of the experimental Rydberg atom array implementation of Maximum Independent Set on unit-disk graphs, including estimation of avoided-crossing location and minimum gap.

algorithm.variant: Rydberg-atom-array adiabatic MIS experiment analyzed perturbatively
algorithm.convergence_criteria: adiabatic evolution in the experimental schedule; theoretical analysis focuses on the avoided crossing

hyperparameters.U: large penalty on independent-set violations in the idealized MIS model

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Rydberg atom array on a square grid; each graph vertex mapped to an atomic qubit
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximum Independent Set on unit-disk graphs
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Rydberg blockade interactions emulate the independent-set penalty
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_Ryd = -delta sum_u n_u + sum_{u,v} V_uv n_u n_v, with H_q = Omega sum_u (|1_u><0_u| + h.c.)

problem_instance.description: Experimental unit-disk graph instances from Ebadi et al. (Science 2022), with n = 39-80 vertices; analyzed via perturbation theory and DMRG.

dataset_specification.description: Programmable Rydberg atom array instances on unit-disk graphs; the paper analyzes the same experimental instances and compares theoretical gap estimates to measured time-to-solution.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: enumerate independent sets of size alpha and alpha-1; build perturbative Hamiltonian H^(2)
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: estimate (Omega/delta)_* and Delta_QAA; compare to experimental time-to-solution

results.unit: Delta_QAA estimated from low-order resolvent / Hamming-distance expansion
(Omega/delta)_* estimated from perturbation theory; agrees better as (Omega/delta)_* becomes small

classical_baselines.unit: O(c^{sqrt(n)}) for unit-disk MIS, c in (1,2)

speedup_claims.conditions: for delocalized instances where the perturbative gap estimate tracks the experimental time-to-solution; optimized QAA on the Rydberg MIS instances
speedup_claims.caveats: some instances are localized and deviate from the square-root-of-SA trend; the analysis is perturbative and compares to experimental TTS rather than directly measuring a quantum runtime

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: theoretical optimized QAA runtime tracks Delta_QAA^{-1}; on delocalized instances Delta_QAA^{-1} ~ sqrt(SA lower bound)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: SA lower bound from D_{alpha-1}/D_alpha; exact classical algorithms scale as O(c^{sqrt(n)}) for unit-disk MIS
